testCase.question: A restaurant proposes a sidewalk café with furniture near a building exit and cellar hatch. The owner says outdoor-dining authorization allows the exterior seats to be counted separately from the interior PACO and eliminates further accessibility review. The documents do not say whether the café is beyond the building line, enclosed, or separated from the interior seating by a Section 713 fire partition. What can be concluded from the selected Building Code passages, and what remains unresolved?
testCase.expectedConclusion: The proposal cannot be approved from the selected evidence. If it is a sidewalk café beyond the building line, BC 3111.1 requires compliance not only with Section 3111 but also with Chapter 32 and separate zoning and agency requirements; the selected evidence does not provide those outside rules. BC 3111.4 prohibits café components from obstructing a building exit or cellar hatch. Its cellar-entrance exception is not automatic: it requires a special application, an easily removable and prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and a cellar entrance or areaway that is not required egress. BC 3111.6 makes Chapter 11 applicable to the café and its access. BC 1108.2.9.1 requires accessible seating and standing spaces equal to at least 10 percent of the total, with not less than one accessible space at each type of dining surface; those spaces must be distributed and located on a level served by an accessible route. BC 3111.7 supplies only a conditional rule for an enclosed sidewalk café: unless a Section 713 fire partition separates it from inside seating, its seating is added to the inside seating solely to determine whether a PACO is required. These passages do not establish the approved interior capacity, the treatment of every open exterior seating arrangement, property-line or operational jurisdiction, DOT authorization, electrical permitting, or overall approval.

expectedUncertainty.description: The selected passages establish several conditional Building Code constraints, but they do not establish overall approval, current agency jurisdiction, lawful seating capacity, or electrical and operational requirements.

answer.answerText:
The owner’s claim is not supported by these passages. If the proposed café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with Building Code Section 3111 but also with the Zoning Resolution, the applicable Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioner requirements, and Chapter 32 projection limits. Thus, an outdoor-dining authorization does not, on this evidence, displace those separate requirements.

For a sidewalk café, furniture, equipment, enclosures, removable platforms, and similar items may not obstruct a building exit or a cellar access hatch/areaway. The only supplied exception for covering a cellar entrance or areaway is conditional: upon special application, the commissioner may permit an easily removable, prominently designated platform designed under Section 3111.5, and only where that entrance or areaway is not used as a required means of egress. The submitted geometry is therefore insufficient to determine compliance at the exit and hatch.

Accessibility review is not eliminated: sidewalk cafés and their access must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces, with at least one of each type of dining surface, must be accessible, distributed throughout the facility, and on a level reached by an accessible route. The supplied evidence does not establish the total or types of dining surfaces, their accessible locations, or the access route, so a compliant accessible count and distribution cannot be determined.

Exterior seats are not automatically counted separately for the stated assembly-seating issue. If the café is enclosed, its seating must be added to the indoor seating when determining whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, unless the two are separated by fire partitions complying with Section 713. Because enclosure status and the claimed fire-partition separation are unknown, the applicable counting result remains unresolved. The supplied passage does not state a corresponding aggregation rule for an unenclosed café.
answer.conclusion: The owner’s claim is not supported by these passages. If the proposed café is beyond the building line, it must comply not only with Building Code Section 3111 but also with the Zoning Resolution, the applicable Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation commissioner requirements, and Chapter 32 projection limits. Thus, an outdoor-dining authorization does not, on this evidence, displace those separate requirements.

supportedPoints.heading: Beyond-building-line cafés remain subject to multiple requirements
supportedPoints.explanation: A sidewalk café provided beyond the building line must comply with Section 3111, the New York City Zoning Resolution, the commissioners of the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection and Department of Transportation, and Chapter 32 projection limitations. The supplied rule does not support treating an outdoor-dining authorization as replacing those requirements.

supportedPoints.heading: Café items cannot obstruct exits or cellar access
supportedPoints.explanation: No awning, enclosure, fixture, equipment, or removable platform of a sidewalk café may obstruct a building exit or a cellar access hatch or areaway. A conditional exception allows the commissioner, upon special application, to permit a qualifying removable and designated platform over a cellar entrance or areaway only if it is not used as a required means of egress and the platform is designed in accordance with Section 3111.5.

supportedPoints.heading: Accessibility remains required
supportedPoints.explanation: Sidewalk cafés and their access must comply with Chapter 11. Where dining surfaces are provided, at least 10 percent of the total seating and standing spaces, but not fewer than one, of each type of dining surface must be accessible, distributed throughout the facility, and located on a level accessed by an accessible route.

supportedPoints.heading: Dining-surface accessibility count and distribution
supportedPoints.explanation: The dining-surface rule establishes a minimum accessible share of the total seating and standing spaces for each type of dining surface and requires distribution throughout the facility and an accessible-route level.

supportedPoints.heading: Enclosed café seating may require aggregation with indoor seating
supportedPoints.explanation: For an enclosed sidewalk café, its seating must be added to indoor seating to determine whether a place-of-assembly certificate of operation is required, unless the seating is separated from the interior by fire partitions complying with Section 713.
